CONTEXT AND CODE. This page belongs to a run of tables (previous page: 149, 157, 173, 181, 197, 229; next page: 853(?), 877, 941, 997, followed by a summary list and an 'Annotatio'). Each block treats a prime p ≡ 5 (mod 8). The header 'p  0.h' gives h = h(-4p), the number of classes of binary forms ax²+2bxy+cy² of determinant b²-ac = -p (Gauss's normalization). The class group is treated as cyclic of order h. 'C.k.(h-k)' denotes the pair formed by the class of index k (k-th power of a generator) and its inverse of index h-k. Gauss writes a single index for the self-inverse classes 0 and h/2. 'c.m' (or 'c:m') records a small first coefficient m of a form in that class. So 'c.1' is the principal form (1,0,p), and 'c.2' is the ambiguous form (2,1,(p+1)/2), which correctly sits at index h/2 every time. For the even indices, i.e. the principal genus, Gauss writes a decomposition p = x²+y²+z².

THE LAW BEING TABULATED (stated on the next page). Let n be the number of essentially distinct decompositions of p (≡5 mod 8) into three squares. Then h = 4n-2, there are 2n inverse-pairs of classes, and the principal genus (the even indices 0,2,...,h-2) contains 2n-1 classes forming exactly n inverse-pairs. So each pair corresponds to one decomposition. This is the case p≡5 (8) of r3(p) = 12·h(-4p) (Disq. Arith. art. 291-292), with the correspondence between representations and principal-genus classes of art. 278ff.

results.what: Class numbers h(-4p) for p = 229, 269, 277, 293, 317, 349, 373 (10, 22, 6, 18, 10, 14, 10), with the cyclic class group laid out by index and inverse pairs, and small-coefficient representatives of odd classes.
results.modern_name: Class group of binary quadratic forms of discriminant -4p (cyclic structure, generator powers)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801, art. 305-307 on cyclic class groups and tables)

results.what: For primes p≡5 mod 8, h(-4p)=4n-2 where n = number of distinct decompositions of p into three squares; principal genus has 2n-1 classes = n inverse pairs, each matched to a decomposition.
results.modern_name: Gauss's three-square theorem r3(p)=12h(-4p) and the correspondence between ternary representations and principal-genus classes

deep.surprise_reason: These are numerical tables illustrating Gauss's own published three-square/class-number theorem (DA art. 291-292) and his work on cyclic class groups. They are worked-out examples of known Gaussian results, with one arithmetic slip.
